guide.summary: Chinese picks the verb and the word order by whether the thing is new or already known. New, indefinite thing: start with the place and put the thing last (Place + 有 / V着 / V了 + a thing). Known, definite thing: put it first and locate it with 在. 是 after a place identifies what occupies it. A place is a noun plus a location word (桌子上), never an English-style preposition phrase.

subs.label: Place + 有 + a new thing
subs.focus: Cue is 'there is/are' + indefinite noun (一本书, 很多人): force 有 (not 在/是) and place-first order. Classic errors: indefinite noun first (一本书在桌子上), 在 as the verb after the place. Never hinge an item on whether 在 may precede the place (variable).

subs.label: Known thing + 在 + place
subs.focus: Cue locates a clearly definite thing (我的, 那本, a name, 'the bank') or asks 在哪儿: force 在 and thing-first order. Classic errors: place + 有 + definite thing (桌子上有我的手机 for 'my phone is on the table'), dropping 在.

subs.label: Place + 是 + what is there
subs.focus: Force 是 against 有/在 when the sentence names what occupies a known spot. 有 must be impossible: use a definite or named occupant (我旁边是小王), 都是/全是, or 是什么地方/是谁. Classic error: 在 after the place (学校对面在银行).

subs.label: When 上 / 里 is needed
subs.focus: Decide if 上/里 must follow the noun: objects need one (在桌子上, 在包里), cities and countries never take 里 (在北京), 上 for surfaces, vehicles, 墙, 黑板. Classic errors: 在桌子, 在冰箱, 在北京里. Do not test 里 after 学校, 公司, 家, 图书馆, 医院 (optional).

subs.label: Noun first, location word after
subs.focus: Force reference noun + location word (学校旁边, 椅子下面, 我后面) and the right word for the cue (旁边 前面 后面 中间 对面 附近 外面 下面). Classic errors: English order (旁边学校, 在前面我), 的 after 上/里 (桌子的上). Do not test optional 的 (学校的旁边 is fine).

subs.label: Place + V着 + a thing
subs.focus: Force Place + V着 + number-measure + noun (门口站着一个人) and 着 over 了/在/过. Classic errors: indefinite noun first (一个人站着在门口), 着 misplaced or missing. Verbs: 站 坐 躺 住 放 挂 写 画 贴 停 摆. Affirmative items only.

subs.label: Place / time + V了 + a new arrival
subs.focus: Force the newcomer after the verb: Place/time + 来/走/搬来/搬走/出现 + 了 + number-measure + noun (我们班来了一个新同学), against the expected definite one before the verb (客人来了). Classic error: place last as in English (一个新同学来了我们班).

subs.label: 没有 and 不在
subs.focus: Force 没有 for 'there is no X' and 不在 for 'X is not there'. Classic errors: 不有, number-measure after 没有 in a plain negative (桌子上没有一本书), negating the wrong verb (他没有家 for 'not at home'). Never offer 没在 as a distractor: it overlaps with 不在.

rules.rule: To say 'there is / there are', start with the place and put the new thing after 有. The thing is indefinite: a number and measure word, 很多, 几, or a bare noun.

examples.py: zhuō zi shàng yǒu yī běn shū
examples.en: There is a book on the table.

examples.py: xué xiào páng biān yǒu yī gè gōng yuán
examples.en: There is a park next to the school.

examples.py: wǒ jiā fù jìn yǒu hěn duō fàn guǎn
examples.en: There are a lot of restaurants near my home.

examples.py: zhè r fù jìn yǒu méi yǒu yín háng
examples.en: Is there a bank near here?

rules.note: The place normally stands at the start without 在. 在桌子上有一本书 is heard, but the bare place is the standard form. A definite noun after 有 is possible only when listing what a place contains (我家有爸爸、妈妈和我), not when saying where a known thing is.

rules.rule: To say where a known thing or person is, put it first and use 在 as the verb. 'The', 'my', 'that', a name or a pronoun in English means 在, not 有.

examples.py: nǐ de shǒu jī zài zhuō zi shàng
examples.en: Your phone is on the table.

examples.py: xiǎo wáng zài jiào shì lǐ
examples.en: Xiao Wang is in the classroom.

examples.py: yín háng zài chāo shì duì miàn
examples.en: The bank is across from the supermarket.

examples.py: wǒ de shū zài nǎ r
examples.en: Where is my book?

rules.rule: Use Place + 是 when you are naming what occupies a spot rather than announcing that something exists there. The thing after 是 can be definite, and 都是 / 全是 means the place is full of it.

examples.py: xué xiào duì miàn shì yī jiā yín háng
examples.en: Across from the school is a bank.

examples.py: wǒ páng biān shì xiǎo wáng
examples.en: The person next to me is Xiao Wang.

examples.py: zhuō zi shàng dōu shì shū
examples.en: The table is covered in books.

examples.py: qián miàn shì shén me dì fang
examples.en: What is that place up ahead?

rules.note: With an indefinite noun both verbs are often possible: 学校对面有一家银行 says a bank exists there (perhaps among other things); 学校对面是一家银行 says the thing over there is a bank. Only 是 works when the occupant is definite or a named person.

rules.rule: An ordinary object is not a place by itself. Add 上 for a surface and 里 for an inside before it can follow 在 or start an existence sentence.

examples.py: niú nǎi zài bīng xiāng lǐ
examples.en: The milk is in the fridge.

examples.py: dì tú zài qiáng shàng
examples.en: The map is on the wall.

examples.py: bāo lǐ yǒu liǎng gè píng guǒ
examples.en: There are two apples in the bag.

examples.py: tā zài huǒ chē shàng kàn shū
examples.en: He is reading on the train.

rules.note: Chinese uses 上 where English says 'in' or 'on' for vehicles and flat things you read: 在飞机上, 在公共汽车上, 在黑板上, 在报纸上. A person is made into a place with 这儿 / 那儿: 你的书在我这儿.

rules.rule: City and country names are already places: never add 里 after them. Buildings and institutions (学校, 公司, 家, 图书馆, 医院) are places too, so 里 is optional with them.

examples.py: tā zài běi jīng gōng zuò
examples.en: He works in Beijing.

examples.py: wǒ jiě jie xiàn zài zài shàng hǎi
examples.en: My older sister is in Shanghai now.

examples.py: zhōng guó yǒu hěn duō dà chéng shì
examples.en: There are many big cities in China.

rules.note: 他在学校 and 他在学校里 are both correct; 里 only stresses 'inside the grounds'.

rules.rule: The location word comes after the noun it refers to, the reverse of English: 'next to the school' is 学校旁边. 上 and 里 attach directly with no 的.

examples.py: māo zài yǐ zi xià miàn
examples.en: The cat is under the chair.

examples.zh: 超市在银行和书店中间。
examples.py: chāo shì zài yín háng hé shū diàn zhōng jiān
examples.en: The supermarket is between the bank and the bookshop.

examples.py: xiǎo wáng zuò zài wǒ hòu miàn
examples.en: Xiao Wang sits behind me.

examples.py: jiào shì wài miàn yǒu hěn duō xué shēng
examples.en: There are a lot of students outside the classroom.

rules.note: Two-syllable location words may take 的 (学校的旁边), but it is usually left out. A location word can also stand alone as a place: 前面有一家咖啡店.

rules.rule: To say how something is sitting, standing, hanging or lying somewhere, replace 有 with a posture or placement verb plus 着. The order stays place first, new thing last.
rules.pattern: Place + Verb + 着 + number + measure + Noun

examples.py: mén kǒu zhàn zhe yī gè rén
examples.en: There is someone standing at the door.

examples.py: qiáng shàng guà zhe yī zhāng dì tú
examples.en: There is a map hanging on the wall.

examples.py: zhuō zi shàng fàng zhe liǎng bēi kā fēi
examples.en: There are two cups of coffee on the table.

rules.note: If the thing is definite it goes first and the pattern changes to Verb + 在: 那张地图挂在墙上.

rules.rule: When someone or something new turns up or leaves, the newcomer goes after the verb. A place or a time word opens the sentence, and the verb takes 了.
rules.pattern: Place / Time + Verb + 了 + number + measure + Noun

examples.zh: 我们班来了一个新同学。
examples.py: wǒ men bān lái le yī gè xīn tóng xué
examples.en: A new classmate has joined our class.

examples.py: zuó tiān lái le yī wèi kè rén
examples.en: A guest came yesterday.

examples.py: lóu shàng bān zǒu le yī jiā rén
examples.en: A family has moved out from upstairs.

rules.note: Position shows whether the person is expected: 客人来了 means the guests (the ones we were waiting for) have arrived; 来客人了 or 来了一位客人 means a guest has turned up. Only verbs of appearing and disappearing work here (来, 走, 搬来, 搬走, 开来, 出现).

rules.rule: 'There is no X' is Place + 没有 + bare noun. 有 is never negated with 不, and the noun loses its number and measure word.

examples.py: zhuō zi shàng méi yǒu shū
examples.en: There are no books on the table.

examples.py: bīng xiāng lǐ méi yǒu niú nǎi le
examples.en: There is no milk left in the fridge.

examples.py: zhè r fù jìn méi yǒu dì tiě zhàn
examples.en: There is no subway station near here.

rules.note: In speech 没有 is often shortened to 没 before the noun: 家里没人. To stress 'not even one', use 一 + measure + noun + 也没有: 桌子上一本书也没有.

rules.rule: 'X is not at the place' is 不在. Choose the negative by the verb the positive sentence would use: 有 becomes 没有, 在 becomes 不在.

examples.py: tā bù zài jiā
examples.en: He is not at home.

examples.py: nǐ de shǒu jī bù zài zhuō zi shàng
examples.en: Your phone is not on the table.

examples.zh: 李老师现在不在办公室。
examples.py: lǐ lǎo shī xiàn zài bù zài bàn gōng shì
examples.en: Teacher Li is not in the office right now.

rules.note: 不在 works for the past as well (他昨天不在家). 没在 is also heard for a past occasion (他昨天没在家), so the two overlap there; 不在 is the safe choice.

right.py: zhuō zi shàng yǒu yī běn shū
right.en: There is a book on the table.

contrasts.why: A new, indefinite thing cannot open the sentence as the subject of 在. Start with the place and introduce the thing after 有.

right.py: nǐ de shǒu jī zài zhuō zi shàng
right.en: Your phone is on the table.

contrasts.why: 你的手机 is a known thing whose location is the news, so it goes first with 在. 有 introduces something the listener has not heard about.

right.py: xué xiào duì miàn shì yín háng
right.en: Across from the school is the bank.

contrasts.why: 在 needs the thing before it and the place after it. When the place comes first, the verb is 是 (identifying) or 有 (existing).

right.py: niú nǎi zài bīng xiāng lǐ
right.en: The milk is in the fridge.

contrasts.why: 冰箱 is an object, not a place. It needs 里 before it can follow 在.

right.py: wǒ zài běi jīng gōng zuò

contrasts.why: English 'in' is already covered by 在. City and country names never take 里.

right.py: yín háng zài xué xiào páng biān
right.en: The bank is next to the school.

contrasts.why: The location word follows its reference noun: 学校旁边, not the English order 'next to the school'.

right.py: jiào shì lǐ méi yǒu rén
right.en: There is nobody in the classroom.

contrasts.why: 有 is only ever negated with 没. 不有 does not exist.

right.py: mén kǒu zhàn zhe yī gè rén
right.en: There is someone standing at the door.

contrasts.why: An unknown person is introduced after the verb: place first, then 站着, then 一个人. 着 is not followed by 在 + place.

contrasts.wrong: 一个新同学来了我们班。

right.zh: 我们班来了一个新同学。
right.py: wǒ men bān lái le yī gè xīn tóng xué
right.en: A new classmate has joined our class.

contrasts.why: The place cannot trail after 来了 the way it does in English. The place opens the sentence and the newcomer follows the verb.

cheat: 'There is a ...'? Place first, then 有, then the thing.
'The / my / that ...' or a name? Thing first, then 在 + place.
Place first and you are naming what it is (or 都是)? Use 是, never 在.
Object after 在? Add 上 or 里. City or country? No 里.
Location word goes after the noun: 学校旁边, 桌子下面, 我后面.
New thing standing, hanging, lying, arriving? Place + V着 / V了 + 一 + measure + noun.
Positive has 有: 没有 + bare noun. Positive has 在: 不在.
